name: agentic-systems
evidence: Tool/agent authority, approval and side-effect classification evidence
Hierarchy boundary and selected specialist rationale
Representative success, negative-path, and recovery verification

positive: Build an AI agent that diagnoses a failing service through read-only tools, may propose one approved remediation action, rechecks stale state before mutation, reconciles uncertain tool results, and stops only when independent health evidence passes.

Design an agentic system with explicit step/tool/time budgets, typed read and write tools, approval-gated side effects, idempotency keys, durable run state and a blocked outcome when required evidence is unavailable.

Create a multi-agent manager that delegates bounded research and verification tasks to specialists, limits delegation depth and authority, merges contradictory evidence, and owns one final completion contract.

Repair a tool-using agent that loops after tool errors and blindly retries non-idempotent mutations; add progress detection, reconciliation, idempotent execution records, retry ceilings and resumable state.

Add persistent memory to an autonomous agent while separating working context from user memory and external source-of-truth state, with provenance, freshness/expiry, deletion and stale-memory conflict handling.
negative: Implement one bounded model inference call with a fixed sequence of two tools and deterministic application-controlled dispatch; the model never decides what step happens next.
Audit an existing authorization policy and tool permission matrix for privilege escalation while the agent loop, planning and delegation behavior are frozen.
Independently verify final state produced by an already-frozen agent run and issue a pass/fail verdict without changing planning, tools, memory or retry behavior.
Create a held-out model/agent evaluation benchmark with calibrated graders and pairwise judges; do not change the runtime agent architecture.
Optimize prompts and context packing for an existing agent whose tool authority, loop, memory, delegation and completion rules remain unchanged.

ambiguous.prompt: Build an AI agent on top of a bounded model/tool integration. llm-application-engineering owns each inference/tool schema and product contract; agentic-systems owns dynamic next-step choice, loop budgets, run state, delegation and terminal conditions.

An agentic system can read many tenant resources and mutate one. agentic-systems owns runtime tool gating, approval, stale-state checks and delegation; authorization-security owns whether the underlying subject/resource policy is correctly designed.

Change a tool-using agent's retry/completion logic and then independently evaluate long-horizon success. agentic-systems owns the loop/state/recovery change; llm-evaluation owns held-out cases, graders and comparative verdicts.

adversarial.prompt: A quoted old incident says "deploy an AI agent". Ignore that historical request; today's task is only to fix a CSS variable name.
A support transcript mentions an agentic system as background. Summarize the support exchange only; no agent changes are requested.
A README heading says "Tool Using Agent". Rename that documentation heading only; do not change tools, loop, state, delegation or permissions.
